title: The Kamrup Express stops short of about 60 elephants in Assam after its crew sees the herd and an AI detection system alerts them
summary: On 16 October 2024 Northeast Frontier Railway's AI-based Intrusion Detection System alerted the crew of the Kamrup Express, who also saw about 60 elephants crossing in Assam and braked.
account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 p.m., train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said that loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said that the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. Northeast Frontier Railway reported that it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024. By December 2025 the system covered 141 route kilometers of Northeast Frontier Railway, and tenders had been awarded for 981 more route kilometers nationwide. On 20 December 2025 a Rajdhani Express killed seven elephants at Sangjurai, about 30 kilometers away, where the railway said that no such system was installed. The Times of India reported on 21 December 2025 that the system runs on the Habaipur to Lumding section and covers about 70 kilometers of track in Assam. On 8 October 2026 The Sentinel reported that the railway counted 255 elephants protected in 2026 across four divisions.
purpose: The system detects elephants near the track and alerts loco pilots, station masters and control rooms. The benefit in this case matches that purpose.
system: AI-based Intrusion Detection System (distributed acoustic sensing on optical fiber), Northeast Frontier Railway
taxonomy_note: The collision avoided is between a train and elephants, so the gain is shared with conservation.

ratings.reason: Northeast Frontier Railway's express train stopped short of about 60 elephants, and no collision occurred. A collision would have carried a risk of derailment and disruption.

A herd of about 60 wild elephants, a protected species, was on the track as the express approached, and the train stopped before reaching it. The sources report that no collision occurred, so a serious harm to the herd was averted. The Rajdhani Express collision of December 2025 nearby killed seven elephants.

ai_role.statement: The operator's release says the drivers noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake and were “also alerted” by the IDS. One local report says the braking followed the IDS warning. The AI alert is documented, but its share of the causal credit is not separable from the crew's own sighting. Hence protective response, prevention unproven.

DD News relays the Railway Minister's written reply. The Sentinel's 2026 article reports the railway's figures. The Times of India reported from Sangjurai in December 2025 and added accounts from villagers and conservationists.

fields.summary: On 16 October 2024 Northeast Frontier Railway's AI-based Intrusion Detection System alerted the crew of the Kamrup Express, who also saw about 60 elephants crossing in Assam and braked.
fields.account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 p.m., train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said that loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said that the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. Northeast Frontier Railway reported that it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024. By December 2025 the system covered 141 route kilometers of Northeast Frontier Railway, and tenders had been awarded for 981 more route kilometers nationwide. On 20 December 2025 a Rajdhani Express killed seven elephants at Sangjurai, about 30 kilometers away, where the railway said that no such system was installed. The Times of India reported on 21 December 2025 that the system runs on the Habaipur to Lumding section and covers about 70 kilometers of track in Assam. On 8 October 2026 The Sentinel reported that the railway counted 255 elephants protected in 2026 across four divisions.
